first_soda.title: The original TAsty SodA Can
first_soda.description:
This can is the first one ever made for the world-renowned Tasty Soda line. With its debut in the 1950s, this is the original can design for the drink.
		The creator of this drink, Johnson P., had a running joke within his circle of friends due to his tendencies to [b] always write with capital A[/b], causing it to be present on the drink.
		It is also important to know that, at the time, many drinks were made of less 'manufactured' ingredients, causing the brand to proudly display their [b] 100% chemical usage [/b]
		An important design choice was the [b] red borders on the outer edges [/b] of the can, allowing others to see its signature [b] bright red look [/b], rather than it being covered by hand.

burger_mascot.title: Antique MC. Duckson Mascot prop
burger_mascot.description:
Deriving from the Original MC. Duckson resturant back in 1942, this prop was loccated on the signage of the building, eventually becoming the main mascot for the resturant chain.
		Sadly, the chain has since discontinued the usage of the mascot, causing memorabilia to be widely desired by nostalgic grown-ups.
		The design of the character is incredibly simple, being a [b] blue dinosaur [/b] with a [b] burger hat [/b]. The eyes on this character are [b] pitch black with no pupils [/b]

burger_toy_car.title: Antique MC. Duckson toy (Car)
burger_toy_car.description:
Many copies of this toy have since been lost to time after the various incidents of melting plastic, causing the rarity to spike. 
		This toy was inside of the classic 'Burgertastic dino toy' line, dating 1943 to 1947, before being switched out for a new, much less popular set.
		It features the titular [b] blue dinosaur [/b] with a [b] burger hat [/b], driving a [b] simplistic red car [/b]. The remaining unopened windows on the car are an interesting [b] green color [/b] that, likely due to a limited color pallete, was chosen to not suggest the dinosaur character was incredibly large.
		[b] Keep an eye out for any melted plastic! We wish for most well-preserved versions of these toys! [/b]
